docs.text: Welcome to NOMAD Gallery — a space to showcase innovative features, uploads, and use cases created with the NOMAD platform. Whether you want to share your latest work or explore what’s possible, this is the place to engage, discover, and inspire. Featured highlights Hand-picked examples that demonstrate what's possible with NOMAD — from large-scale databases to innovative workflows. PERLA – The PERovskite Photovoltaics Living Archive on NOMAD Photovoltaics View in Gallery The Catalysis App Catalysis View in Gallery Martignac: High-Throughput Martini Workflows with NOMAD Integration Computational Soft Matter and Biomolecular Simulation View in Gallery Explore the NOMAD Gallery Browse community-submitted use cases showing how NOMAD is used in real research workflows. Use the filters below to explore by methodology, research field, or keywords. Methodology Research field Country Keywords 0 of 0 Sort: Newest Clear Connecting NOMAD and Galaxy: An EOSC Data Analysis Workflow Humboldt-Universität zu Berlin, Universität Freiburg • DE Materials Science Workflows Mixed/Hybrid Scientific data may be stored and managed in one platform while specialized analysis tools and workflows are available in another. This demonstrator shows how NOMAD can connect to the open-source data analysis platform Galaxy within the emerging EOSC federation, allowing data stored in NOMAD to be sent to an external analysis workflow and the results returned to NOMAD. Using XPS peak finding as an example, a NOMAD Action transfers an XPS dataset to Galaxy, launches a dedicated workflow, retrieves the processed result, and reimports it into the original NOMAD upload. #XPS #Workflows #NOMAD Actions #NeXus By Lukas Pielsticker 2026-10-08 View Details Technique XPS Contributors Lukas Pielsticker, Björn Grüning, Michael Krieger, Heiko Weber, Claudia Draxl Publication References https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23110600 Repository References https://github.com/FAIRmat-NFDI/nomad-eosc-galaxy-actions/ NOMAD Resource Links https://nomad-lab.eu/oasis-b/projects/6YTLTyKaRpqunYzYSxkgXA Funding References Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft (DFG) - Project 460197019 XAS Data Across Facilities: From Semantic Search to Analysis with NOMAD Humboldt-Universität zu Berlin, European Synchrotron Radiation Facility (ESRF), Helmholtz-Zentrum Berlin (HZB) • DE, FR Experimental Materials Science Experimental Experimental data are generated across facilities using different formats, catalogues, and terminology, making it difficult to discover and reuse data consistently. This demonstrator connects data sources through shared semantic concepts and standardized representations in NOMAD. Using X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) data from ESRF and BESSY II as an example, it shows how data can be discovered across facilities, brought into a common representation, and processed with shared data analysis workflows. #XAS #Ontologies #Semantic search #Synchrotrons #Interoperability By Lukas Pielsticker 2026-10-08 View Details Technique XAS Contributors Lukas Pielsticker, Tanmay Kulkarni, Heike Görzig, Sonal Patel, Giannis Koumoutsos, Michael Krieger, Heiko Weber, Sandor Brockhauser, Claudia Draxl Publication References https://oscars-project.eu/projects/findable-big-data-various-material-characterisation-techniques-0 Repository References https://github.com/FAIRmat-NFDI/nomad-semantic-web-service https://github.com/FAIRmat-NFDI/nomad-ontology-service https://github.com/FAIRmat-NFDI/pynxtools-xas NOMAD Resource Links https://nomad-lab.eu/oasis-b/projects/R5NsPg3ITxuaNvY-6xNgcA Funding References Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft (DFG) - Project 460197019 Horizon Europe - Project 101129751 Martignac: High-Throughput Martini Workflows with NOMAD Integration Universität Heidelberg, Humboldt-Universität zu Berlin • DE Computational Soft Matter and Biomolecular Simulation Computational Martignac is a workflow library for coarse-grained molecular simulations based on the Martini force field. It supports a range of standard free-energy and high-throughput simulation applications, including solvation studies, membrane permeation calculations, and molecular property screening. By integrating workflow automation with the NOMAD data management platform, Martignac enables highthroughput simulation workflows while ensuring reproducibility and provenance tracking through FAIR data management. In particular, simulations are represented as composable workflows that automatically reuse previously generated data by retrieving existing results from NOMAD on the fly. #Martini #Molecular dynamics #Coarse-grained simulation #High-throughput screening #FAIR data #Workflow automation #Molecular discovery #Biomolecular simulation #Reproducibility By Joseph Rudzinski 2026-06-15 View Details Technique Martini Coarse-Grained Molecular Dynamics, High-Throughput Molecular Simulation Contributors Tristan Bereau, Luis J. Walter, Joseph F. Rudzinski Publication References https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.jcim.4c01754 Repository References https://github.com/tbereau/martignac/ NOMAD Resource Links https://doi.org/10.17172/NOMAD/2024.10.01-1 https://doi.org/10.17172/NOMAD/2024.09.25-1 Funding References Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft (DFG) - Project 390900948 Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft (DFG) - Project 460197019 Novel Materials Synthesis at the DTU Nanolab Technical University of Denmark • DK Novel Materials Synthesis Experimental High-throughput and autonomous experimentation generate complex, heterogeneous datasets whose reuse, large-scale analysis, and linking to data from first-principles calculations remain challenging. We use the NOMAD Oasis data infrastructure as a digital backbone for daily high-throughput experimental work in our materials discovery group at DTU Nanolab. The customized platform supports the complete experimental workflow in a thin-film laboratory, linking physical inventory items, automated synthesis logs, high-throughput characterization data, and cloud-based analysis within a unified data model. Our NOMAD Oasis installation preserves full sample provenance across multi-step workflows and uses unified sample coordinates to enable direct cross-technique correlation. We demonstrate the capabilities of the platform on a combined experimental-computational project centered on phosphosulfide thin-film libraries. The data consists of 12,000 experimental samples acquired during routine operation over 18 months, complemented by more than 800 first-principles calculations – all managed in a unified data platform available on NOMAD . We show how an open, extensible data infrastructure system supports reproducible workflows, scalable analysis, and long-term data reuse. #Novel materials #Synthesis #Combinatorial #Thin films By Hampus Näsström 2026-06-15 View Details Technique Combinatorial Synthesis and High-Throughput Characterization Contributors Lena A Mittmann, Hampus Nässtrom, Eugène Bertin, Sarthak Kapoor, Inês Diogo, Anat Itzhak, Giulia Dalmonte, Rasmus Thorup Danielsen, Malthe E. Skytte, Holger Von Wenckstern, Andrea Crovetto, José A Márquez Publication References https://doi.org/10.26434/chemrxiv.15000115/v2 Repository References https://github.com/DTU-Nanolab-materials-discovery/nomad-dtu-nanolab-plugin https://github.com/DTU-Nanolab-materials-discovery/nomad-oasis-image NOMAD Resource Links https://nomad.nanolab.dtu.dk/nomad-oasis/gui/search/combinatorial-samples Funding References VILLUM FONDEN - Research Grant 42140 European Union (ERC) - IDOL, Grant 101040153 Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft (DFG) - Project 460197019 Media URLs https://dtu-nanolab-materials-discovery.github.io/nomad-dtu-nanolab-plugin/ Alexandria Database Integration and Search App Ruhr-Universität Bochum, Humboldt-Universität zu Berlin • DE Computational Materials Science Computational The Alexandria Materials Database is a large, open high-throughput database of density-functional theory (DFT) calculations covering millions of predicted materials across 1D, 2D, and 3D chemical spaces. Alexandria is integrated into NOMAD through a dedicated search application that enables efficient exploration of the raw data using NOMAD's powerful search, filtering, visualization, and analysis tools. Researchers can rapidly identify materials of interest, investigate structure–property relationships, and access FAIR computational materials data at scale. The integration currently provides access to more than 2 million Alexandria entries within the NOMAD ecosystem and continues to grow. #Materials database #High-throughput calculations #PBEsol #PBE By Joseph Rudzinski 2026-06-15 View Details Technique DFT Contributors Silvana Botti, Martin Kuban, Miguel A.L. Marques, Joseph F. Rudzinski Publication References https://doi.org/10.1016/j.mtphys.2024.101560 https://alexandria.icams.rub.de/ Repository References https://github.com/FAIRmat-NFDI/nomad-app-plugins-simulation NOMAD Resource Links https://nomad-lab.eu/prod/v1/gui/search/alexandria Funding References Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft (DFG) - Project 460197019 The Perovskite Solar Cell App Humboldt-Universität zu Berlin • DE Photovoltaics Experimental The Perovskite Solar Cell App provides a domain-specific search interface within NOMAD that allows users to explore perovskite photovoltaic data using rich metadata and interactive filters. Researchers can search by absorber composition, device structure, processing conditions, efficiency metrics, and many other parameters, enabling rapid discovery, benchmarking, and data-driven analysis. The app is powered by FAIR data models and the NOMAD Perovskite Solar Cell Database infrastructure. The app transforms a large collection of perovskite photovoltaic data into a searchable and reusable research resource. By making historical and newly contributed data FAIR and interoperable, it enables benchmarking, trend analysis, machine learning applications, and accelerated discovery in photovoltaic materials research. #Perovskite #Solar cells #Energy materials #Materials database By Ahmed Mansour 2026-06-15 View Details Data Size 1.5 TB Technique Perovskite Solar Cell Fabrication, Photovoltaic Device Characterization Contributors José A. Márquez Prieto, Hampus Näsström, Lev Ginzburg, Sherjeel Shabih, Yaru Wang, Fabian Schöppach, Haoyu Yang, Adam Fekete, Lauri Himanen, Sharat Patil, Jesper Jacobsson, Kevin Jablonka Publication References https://zenodo.org/doi/10.5281/zenodo.17358042 https://www.nature.com/articles/s41560-021-00941-3 Repository References https://github.com/FAIRmat-NFDI/nomad-perovskite-solar-cells-database NOMAD Resource Links https://nomad-lab.eu/prod/v1/staging/gui/search/perovskite-solar-cells-database Funding References Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft (DFG) - Project 460197019 Horizon Europe - Project 101122288 Media URLs https://fairmat-nfdi.github.io/nomad-perovskite-solar-cells-database/ NOMAD CAMELS Plugin – Parser and Search App Humboldt-Universität zu Berlin • DE Experimental Physics Experimental The NOMAD CAMELS Plugin allows users to automatically parse all measurement files (HDF5) recorded with NOMAD CAMELS . Parsing creates a NOMAD entry out of every CAMELS measurement file. This makes metadata that users entered or that was automatically recorded by CAMELS searchable in NOMAD (Oasis). The CAMELS App allows you to easily filter all your NOMAD CAMELS entries. Quickly find your measurement data by filtering on the following metadata: Measurements start time Measurements end time Session Tags Measurement description Comments Protocol description Protocol overview User Sample #Experiment #NOMAD app #Parser #NOMAD CAMELS By Alexander Fuchs 2026-06-05 View Details Contributors Alexander Fuchs, Johannes Lehmeyer, Heiko Weber, Michael Krieger Publication References https://joss.theoj.org/papers/10.21105/joss.06371 Repository References https://github.com/FAIRmat-NFDI/nomad-camels-plugin https://github.com/FAU-LAP/NOMAD-CAMELS Funding References Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft (DFG) - Project 460197019 Media URLs https://youtube.com/playlist?list=PLrRaxjvn6FDWR-8SWOfy0j7ux5u3TF_VJ&si=nZZq3C2FhBqdL7Vg PERLA – The PERovskite Photovoltaics Living Archive on NOMAD Humboldt-Universität zu Berlin, Friedrich Schiller University Jena • DE Photovoltaics Experimental PERLA transforms perovskite solar cell literature into a living, continuously updated knowledge resource. Through AI-powered data extraction and FAIR data management workflows, PERLA converts scientific publications into structured, reusable data accessible through NOMAD. Researchers can explore emerging trends, perform large-scale analyses, and accelerate innovation in next-generation photovoltaic technologies. #Perovskites #Solar cells #Energy materials #Materials database #Large language models #Data extraction By Ahmed Mansour 2026-06-03 View Details Technique AI-Assisted Literature Mining Contributors Sherjeel Shabih, Hampus Näsström, Sharat Patil, Asmin Askin, Keely Dodd-Clements, Jessica Helisa Hautrive Rossato, Hugo Gajardoni de Lemos, Yuxin Liu, Florian Mathies, Natalia Maticiuc, Rico Meitzner, Edgar Nandayapa, Juan José Patiño López, Yaru Wang, Lauri Himanen, Eva Unger, T. Jesper Jacobsson, José A. Márquez, Kevin Maik Jablonka Publication References https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2601.17807 Repository References https://github.com/FAIRmat-NFDI/perla https://github.com/lamalab-org/perla-extract https://github.com/FAIRmat-NFDI/nomad-perovskite-solar-cells-database NOMAD Resource Links https://nomad-lab.eu/prod/v1/staging/gui/search/perovskite-solar-cells-database Funding References Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft (DFG) - Project 460197019 Horizon Europe - Project 101122288 Media URLs https://fairmat-nfdi.github.io/perla/ Battery Database: Literature-mined Battery Properties with Searchable Visualization Humboldt-Universität zu Berlin • DE Battery Science Mixed/Hybrid The Battery Database plugin brings literature-derived battery materials data into NOMAD, where it can be searched, filtered, visualized, and reused. It supports curated experimental battery properties from published papers and provides an interface for exploring materials and properties such as capacity, voltage, conductivity, Coulombic efficiency, and energy. #Battery database #ChemDataExtractor #Literature mining #Materials informatics #Energy density By Udaykumar Gajera 2026-06-03 View Details Data Size 700 MB Technique Literature mining with ChemDataExtractor, followed by parsing, normalization, and visualization in NOMAD Contributors Hampus Näsström, Jose Pizarro Blanco Publication References https://www.nature.com/articles/s41597-020-00602-2 Repository References https://github.com/FAIRmat-NFDI/nomad-battery-database NOMAD Resource Links https://nomad-lab.eu/prod/v1/oasis/gui/search/batterydb Funding References Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft (DFG) - Project 460197019 The Catalysis App Humboldt-Universität zu Berlin, Fritz-Haber-Institut der Max-Planck-Gesellschaft • DE Catalysis Experimental The Catalysis App allows researchers to explore heterogeneous catalysis datasets available in NOMAD through an interactive interface. Users can search and filter data by parameters such as reactants and products, synthesis method, catalyst form, and reaction conditions. The Catalysis App supports the exchange of catalysis data and lays important groundwork for future AI-driven analytics. #Catalysis research #Machine-readable data #NOMAD app By Julia Schumann 2026-05-08 View Details Data Size 2000 entries < Contributors Hampus Näsström, Michael Götte, Lauri Himanen, Abdulrhman Moshanta, Markus Scheidgen, José A. Márquez, Claudia Draxl, Annette Trunschke Publication References https://doi.org/10.1038/s41929-026-01508-9 Repository References https://github.com/FAIRmat-NFDI/nomad-catalysis-plugin NOMAD Resource Links https://nomad-lab.eu/prod/v1/gui/search/heterogeneouscatalyst Funding References Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft (DFG) - Project 460197019

docs.text: Welcome to NOMAD Gallery — a space to showcase innovative features, uploads, and use cases created with the NOMAD platform. Whether you want to share your latest work or explore what’s possible, this is the place to engage, discover, and inspire. Submit your use case We welcome contributions to the NOMAD Gallery! To submit a new entry, simply fill out the submission form . The form will guide you through the required information to ensure your submission follows the correct format. Once submitted, a team member will review your entry to make sure everything looks good and will take care of publishing it. You will receive a confirmation once your submission has been processed. If you have any questions, feel free to reach out through our Discord server or email us .
